title: The Slippery Slope
story: You and NOVA are designing a toy-car track when the workshop locks. NOVA must understand friction before the door will open, because its car keeps either sliding out of control or getting stuck.
escaped: The workshop opens. NOVA now reads friction data, sorts ways to change friction and knows why friction is useful.

locks.title: Which surface stops the car?
locks.intro: A toy car was released from the same ramp onto different surfaces. NOVA measured how far it rolled.
locks.question: What conclusion fits the data?
options: The rougher the surface, the more friction, so the shorter the distance.
The colour of the surface decides the distance.
Friction is the same on every surface.
locks.hint: Put the surfaces in order from smoothest to roughest and compare the distances.
locks.learn: AI finds patterns like this by comparing many results. The pattern matches the science: rough surfaces interlock more, so friction is greater.

locks.title: More friction or less?
locks.intro: NOVA must sort ideas into ways to increase friction and ways to reduce it. Choose its clues.

features.text: Makes surfaces rougher or gives more grip

test.name: Gymnast's coarse powder on the hands

locks.hint: The carrom board and the gymnast both use powder in sport, yet they want opposite things.
locks.learn: 'Used in sports' or 'used on vehicles' says where something is used, not what it does to friction. NOVA needs the clue about grip.

locks.title: Check NOVA's big idea
locks.intro: NOVA has a plan to get rid of friction everywhere. Is it right? Decide and pick the fact that settles it.
locks.claim: Friction is always bad. A world without friction would be better.
evidence: Without friction we couldn't walk, write or hold things; friction is a necessary evil.
Friction depends on how rough the surfaces are.
locks.hint: Could you walk on a floor with no friction at all?
locks.learn: A claim that is partly true (friction wastes energy as heat) can lead to a bad conclusion. Look for the evidence that tests the WHOLE claim.

locks.title: Fix NOVA's notes on fluid friction
locks.intro: NOVA has notes about friction in air and water. Tick the notes that are wrong.

rows.label: Is shaped to reduce fluid friction
Causes no friction on moving things
rows.why: air resistance is a kind of fluid friction

rows.label: Has a body shaped to reduce drag in flight
Doesn't slow swimmers down at all
rows.why: water exerts fluid friction (drag) on swimmers

locks.hint: Fluids are liquids AND gases. Do both of them push back on moving objects?
locks.learn: Absolute words like 'no' and 'at all' in training data are worth double-checking. They are often where the mistakes hide.
